(b) Since you’re near‑sighted and wear prescription glasses, aim for seats a bit closer to the screen but still around the middle row for height. That way you get sharp visuals without needing to tilt your head much, and you’ll catch all the little details in each scene.
(c) A good rule is to pick a seat somewhere near the middle of the theater, both in distance from the screen and in the row order. You’ll get a balanced view and sound without having to crane your neck.
(d) Because you’ve got near‑sightedness and rely on glasses, your sweet spot is usually a few rows closer than the average viewer, roughly mid‑height in the seating layout. It keeps the screen crisp and prevents the constant head-tilt that can mess with your comfort.
